title: Yukon power infrastructure project now at Carney's Major Projects Office

Feds investing $73M in Whitehorse Power Centres
The number-one item on Yukon Premier Currie Dixon's wishlist has materialized: federal support for a major power infrastructure project in the territory.
Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Thursday the Whitehorse Power Centres project has been referred to the federal Major Projects Office.

The announcement came after a day of meetings between the prime minister, Yukon Premier Currie Dixon and First Nations leaders in Whitehorse. Before the visit, Dixon said his top priority was talking with Carney about the territory's electrical grid.

"The Yukon is growing, and reliable, affordable electricity is essential to building our future," Dixon said in a news release Thursday night. He added federal support gives the Yukon a chance to double its electricity grid.

items: What will the federal government's Major Projects Office do — and will it succeed?

blocks.text: The Whitehorse Power Centres project, which will now see a federal investment of up to $73 million, includes two new thermal power plants, a new electrical substation and transmission infrastructure in Whitehorse. It will add 15 megawatts of capacity to the grid by 2028, a number that should eventually expand to 150 megawatts in later phases of the project.
A news release from the Prime Minister's Office states the Major Projects Office will help Yukon assess necessary upgrades to accommodate stress on its power grids as a result of the project.
It said the office will also look at opportunities for Indigenous partners to participate in the energy sector, including through potential equity ownership.

Yukon Energy has said the plants are a necessity right now as the grid is under increasing strain. Last winter, the territory almost maxed out its power capacity during a particularly nasty cold snap, prompting warnings from officials of possible rolling blackouts — though it never actually came to that.

This winter, the territory and City of Whitehorse have said they have a plan to prevent that risk from happening again, by selecting buildings to temporarily disconnect from the grid at times of peak energy demand.

The power project in question was identified in the federal budget earlier this month, but Thursday is the first time the federal government has released a figure for how much funding it intends to apply to it.

The Major Projects Office was established to speed up permitting for projects considered to be in the national interest. Other northern projects include the Mackenzie Valley Highway and Taltson hydro expansion in the N.W.T., and the Grays Bay Port and Road Project in Nunavut.
